notes: Five alternating-order rounds (order rotated and reversed between rounds) on a shared 4-core VM; no concurrent builds or test jobs owned by this experiment (one-minute load 1.0-1.8). Other host activity was uncontrolled.

Base is main 28881e27; candidate is 0c97e13c, the head of the stack of #680 (len() and bytes reads), #682 (subjects read in place), #683 (alternation filter) and the State allocation change, before they merged main e3b53c4c. Each tree used the compiler binary built from its own sources (the SHA-256s below); the candidate's compiler sources are #682's.
JIT runtime caches primed before timing; default optimization and JIT inlining limit (PYSTACHY_JIT_INLINE unset).
All outputs/checksums agreed across CPython, base and candidate in both modes; repeat checksums compared with timings removed.

Timed workloads include in-loop lazy initialization and cache misses. Whole-process time adds setup, checksums, startup and JIT compilation; the candidate compiles the matcher twice (bytes and list[int] subjects), which adds about 0.5 s of JIT compilation per run.
repeat is tools/re_repeat_bench.py 1000 --cpu; each process reports the median of three warmed samples per case.

instruction_counts.tool: valgrind --tool=callgrind (Ir); AOT binaries for base/head, python3.13 -I for cpython
instruction_counts.note: timed_loops = run with loops minus run without loops (setup, checksums and startup cancel). regex_dna's run without loops is a copy that exits after its setup when given 0 loops (the benchmark itself needs one loop). v8_timed is bench/pyperformance/regex_v8.py with the post-loop checksum removed. Callgrind counts each byte of a rep-stosb memset as an instruction, which inflates Pystachy allocation zeroing relative to its time.
